h: Local API server (Anthropic Messages / OpenAI chat) — work log
t:
Goal: let other apps on the device (e.g. Mobile Harness running Claude Code) use the model that is loaded in this app.
Delivered in three steps so each can be built and tested on its own:
| step | content | user-visible? |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | engine patch 0004, JNI `nativeGenerateChat`, `EngineBackend.generateChat`, `EngineController` queue + in-app priority | no |
| **B** | the HTTP server (`/v1/messages`, `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`, ...), `ApiServerService`, server settings in the DataStore | via an `adb` start hook (no screen yet) |
| **C** | Settings screen: on/off, port, key, endpoint URL + copy button, force-server-settings, context, thinking, max tokens | yes |

**Why the stock llama-server is not embedded.** `server_context` loads its own model and runs `llama_decode` itself; that
would bypass `bmoe::Session` (expert streaming, cache, hooks). The server is written in Kotlin on top of the same
`Session`, so every backend path (MoE streaming, dense mmap, optional NPU prefill) is the one the chat already uses.

`GenerateRequest` gets an optional *stateless chat* mode. It is off unless `chat_messages_json` is non-empty, and then
`generate()` is byte-for-byte the old path (the existing tests/CLI/app turn never set it).
* **Messages + tools through the model's own jinja template.** `chat_messages_json` is an OpenAI-format array
  (system/user/assistant/tool, assistant `tool_calls`, tool `tool_call_id`), `chat_tools_json` an OpenAI `tools` array.
  Parsed with llama.cpp's `common_chat_msgs_parse_oaicompat` / `common_chat_tools_parse_oaicompat` and rendered with
  `common_chat_templates_apply` (`use_jinja`, tools, tool_choice, `parallel_tool_calls`).
  Tool calls in the output are parsed by llama.cpp's chat parser and returned in `RunResult::tool_calls`.
  **They are parsed, not grammar-constrained** (the engine has no grammar sampler), so a weak model can still emit a bad call.

* **KV prefix reuse (the priority item).** The KV is *not* cleared. The rendered prompt is tokenised and its longest common
  token prefix with what the KV holds is kept; only the rest is prefilled (this is the existing continued-chat mechanism,
  now reachable without the engine-side chat history). No match, or a KV that cannot drop a tail (some SWA / recurrent
  memories refuse `seq_rm`), simply means a full re-prefill. `RunResult::n_prompt_total` / `n_reused` report what happened.
  A turn cancelled *after* its prefill keeps the prompt in the KV (retry after a client abort or an in-app preemption does
  not pay for it twice); the old behaviour for the app's own turns is unchanged.
* **Stop strings** on the answer text only (never the reasoning). Possible partial matches are held back from the stream.
* **Per-request sampling** (`sampling_override`): temperature/top_p/top_k/seed, built as a request-scoped sampler chain
  (temp <= 0 = greedy). Cheap, so it is supported. Not supported by the engine at all: min_p, repetition/frequency
  penalties, grammar.

* **`max_tokens` is clamped** to the room left in the context instead of failing (Claude Code asks for 32k+).
* `stop_reason`: `end_turn`, `max_tokens`, `stop_sequence` or `tool_use`.
* With tools in the request the "close the reasoning span in the prompt" trick for think=false is not used (a prefilled turn
  bypasses the parser that finds the tool calls). A model whose template ignores `enable_thinking` therefore still reasons
  when tools are present; its reasoning is split out of the answer either way.

* `native-bridge.cpp`: new `nativeGenerateChat` (JSON in; deltas, tool calls (flat id/name/arguments triples), stop reason,
  reuse counters out). `nativeGenerate` is untouched.
* `EngineNativeBridge.kt`: `nativeGenerateChat` + `NativeChatCallback`.
* `EngineBackend.kt`: `generateChat(...)` with a default "unsupported" body, so existing implementations and fakes compile unchanged.
* `ChatApiTypes.kt` (new): `ChatGenRequest`, `SamplingOverride`, `ChatEvent`, `ChatStats`, `ChatToolCall`.
* `EngineController.kt`:
  * `acquireForApi(timeoutMs, maxQueued)` — FIFO queue, one API request at a time, bounded wait; `null` means "answer 529".
  * `generateChat(lease, request)` — the streaming flow; afterwards the in-app chat's engine state key is invalidated, so the
    next in-app turn replays its saved history (same as after Choose-from-options).

* **In-app chat has priority.** If the app starts a generation while an API generation runs, the API generation is cancelled
    (`ChatEvent.Finished.preempted = true`) and the app proceeds once it has unwound. Queued API requests wait until the app is
    idle or their wait runs out (then 529). Everything else the app did before (refusing a second app generation or a
    decide() while busy) is unchanged.

h: RAM cost of a big context (read before enabling the server, step C exposes the setting)
t:
The KV cache is allocated when the model is loaded and grows linearly with the context. Rough size (f16 K and V):
`2 x layers x context x kv_heads x head_dim x 2 bytes`. For a model with 48 layers, 4 KV heads and head_dim 128 (a
Qwen3-30B-A3B-class shape, arithmetic only, not measured here) that is about 3 GiB at 32k tokens and 6 GiB at 64k.
It competes with the expert cache and the OS page cache on the phone. Changing the context size needs a model reload.

h: Status of step A — what was and was not checked
t:
Things I could not verify and would check first on a device: that `common_chat_msgs_parse_oaicompat` accepts the exact
JSON step B produces for your model's template, that prefix reuse actually hits for Claude Code's request shape (step B
normalises the per-request billing header to keep the prefix stable), and the cancel/preempt timing during a long prefill.
---

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `server/Http.kt` | `MiniHttpServer`: a small HTTP/1.1 server on `java.net.ServerSocket` (keep-alive, Content-Length and chunked request bodies, `Expect: 100-continue`, chunked/SSE responses). No new dependency |
| `server/ApiServer.kt` | routing, auth, queue/lease handling, non-streaming and streaming chat, error mapping, `X-BigMoe-Ignored` header |
| `server/AnthropicApi.kt` | Anthropic request -> OpenAI-format engine request (system blocks, tool_use/tool_result, thinking, images -> placeholder), response builder, `AnthropicStreamEncoder` (SSE event sequence) |
| `server/OpenAiApi.kt` | the same for `/v1/chat/completions`, `OpenAiStreamEncoder` |
| `server/ApiRuntime.kt` | per-request settings snapshot and `RequestResolver` ("Force server settings", output cap, thinking default) |
| `server/ApiKey.kt` | key generation, constant-time compare, `x-api-key` / `Authorization: Bearer` |
| `server/ApiServerService.kt` | foreground service (type specialUse, own notification with a Stop action, wake lock only while a request runs, follows the settings) |
| `server/ApiServerController.kt` | on/off + key helpers; `ApiServerIntentHook` (adb test hook) |
| `EngineSettingsDataStore.kt` | server settings, `effectiveContextLength` (see below) |
| `AppContainer.kt`, `OnEdgeApplication.kt`, `MainActivity.kt`, `AndroidManifest.xml` | wiring: controller, autostart when left enabled, the adb hook, the service entry |

* **Binds 127.0.0.1 only** by default; port from settings (default 8080). `serverBindAll` (0.0.0.0) exists in the data layer, and then the key is always required.
* **Auth**: key generated on first start and required by default. `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `x-api-key: <key>` both work. Auth can be turned off only while bound to loopback (`serverRequireKey=false`); `GET /health` never needs a key.
* **Model**: whatever is loaded in the app. The `model` field of a request is accepted and echoed, any name works; `/v1/models` returns the loaded model. No model loaded: HTTP 503.
* **Settings come from the app.** The server has no copies of the app's own settings: context size, Max tokens, Thinking, temperature / top_p / top_k and the MTP / guess-ahead options are the ones from Settings. The only server-specific settings are on/off, port, key, authentication, listen-on-network, "Force server settings" and the queue wait.

* **MTP / n-gram guess-ahead apply to the server.** The server runs on the same engine session the chat uses, and speculation is decided per session (`spec_on` in `Session::generate`, independent of the request kind), so a model loaded with MTP or n-gram speculation drafts for API requests too. Speculation works with sampling: drafts are verified by drawing with the request's own sampler, so client temperature / top_p / top_k apply as without guess-ahead (fewer drafts are accepted at higher temperatures). Not yet measured on a device.
* **Queue / priority**: one request at a time, FIFO, up to `serverQueueTimeoutSec` (default 60 s) of waiting, then HTTP 529 `overloaded_error`. If the in-app chat starts, a *running* API request is cancelled (non-streaming: 529; streaming: an `error` event with `overloaded_error`) and queued ones keep waiting or time out with 529.

* **Streaming**: `stream:true` gives Anthropic SSE (`message_start`, `content_block_*`, `message_delta`, `message_stop`). `event: ping` is sent whenever nothing was written for 3 s, so a long prefill does not hit the client's read timeout. (A non-streaming request cannot be kept alive this way.)
* **Thinking**: with thinking on, reasoning arrives as `thinking` content blocks (`thinking_delta`, empty `signature`), never in the text block; with it off, reasoning is dropped. `thinking.budget_tokens` is not enforced.
* **tool_use**: a tool call is delivered once the engine has parsed it complete: one `content_block_start`, one `input_json_delta` carrying the whole input, one stop. Not token-by-token.
* **Honoured request fields**: `max_tokens` (capped by the app's Max tokens, 0 = no cap; the app default is unlimited (0 = no cap beyond the available context)), `stop_sequences`, `stream`, `system`, `messages`, `tools`, `tool_choice` (`any`/`tool` -> "some tool", a specific tool cannot be forced), `thinking`, and unless forced `temperature` / `top_p` / `top_k` (OpenAI: `seed` too).

* **Force server settings ON**: request sampling, request `thinking` and request `max_tokens` are ignored; the app's own sampler settings, its Thinking switch and its Max tokens apply. `stop_sequences` and `stream` are always honoured.
* **Ignored, and said so**: the response carries `X-BigMoe-Ignored: ...` listing what was not applied (forced values, `budget_tokens`, images, `min_p`, penalties, `n`>1, `response_format`, ...).
* **Images** in requests are replaced by a text placeholder (the stateless path has no vision).
* **Usage**: reused KV prefix is reported as `cache_read_input_tokens`, so `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens` is the whole prompt.
* **count_tokens** is an estimate (about 3 bytes per token), marked with `X-BigMoe-Estimate: true`.
* **Context**: the app's "Context size" (default 4096). Claude Code's first request is far bigger, so set it to 32768 or more and reload the model; the settings section warns while the loaded context is smaller. See the RAM note in step A. A prompt that does not fit is answered with HTTP 400 telling you to raise the context.
* The per-request Claude Code billing stamp (`cch=`) is blanked so the system prompt stays identical across requests and the KV prefix is reused.

* Tool calls are parsed from the model's text, not grammar-constrained; a small model can emit a malformed call (it becomes `{}` input).
* Cancelling a request *during prefill* drops only that request's own prefill progress; once prefill is done a cancel keeps the prompt in the KV.
* A non-streaming request cannot be kept alive during a long prefill and a disconnect is only noticed on streaming requests (pings make the write fail).
* Models whose memory cannot drop a KV tail (some SWA / recurrent ones) get a full re-prefill every request; the log line shows `reused=0`.
* One engine: Claude Code's background "fast model" calls queue behind the main one.

* The API section moved to the bottom of Settings and is collapsible (arrow).
* Removed the duplicate server settings (context size, thinking, max output tokens); the server follows the app's own. Stored values of the removed keys are simply ignored.
* Chat: the status shown before the first token (while the prompt is being read) now says "Reading…" instead of "Thinking…". The real "Thinking" block for reasoning is unchanged.
* `session.cpp`: a turn cancelled after prefill keeps the prompt in the KV only when there is no MTP draft context (otherwise it rolls back as before). Patch 0004 regenerated; `git apply --check` on the pristine tree passed again, `g++ -fsyntax-only` on `session.cpp` and the bridge passed again. Kotlin: still not compiled, tests still never run.

Scope: every file I wrote or touched, every engine `.cpp` (28 files, `g++ -Wall -Wextra`), and a pattern scan of all Kotlin (swallowed cancellation, divisions, global scopes) plus a read of the risky numeric code (GGUF parser, ContextPlanner, calculator, unit converter, workspace path check).
Fixed:
* **Security:** the adb hook (`api_server`, `api_key` extras) lived in the exported `MainActivity`, so any installed app could start the server, choose its key or switch authentication off. It now works in debuggable builds only; `api_no_auth` is removed.
* **Security / DoS:** the HTTP layer read the whole body (up to 64 MB) before checking the key. Auth is now checked on the request head, before the body (`MiniHttpServer.guard`). `/health` no longer reveals the model name.
* Stop button in the notification could leave "server enabled" on (the write ran in the service's own scope, cancelled with the service): now persisted in the app scope.
* Open client connections survived `stop()` (a blocking read cannot be cancelled): all sockets are closed on stop.

* An in-app generation that asked for the engine in the instant between an API lease being granted and its native call started was missed (the native side clears its cancel flag on start): `generateChat` now checks the lease and the token callback keeps checking it.
* `max_tokens` <= 0 was passed on to the engine, where it means "fill the whole context": now a 400, like Anthropic.
* Claude Code's billing-header system block (changes every request, useless to a local model) is dropped instead of kept with a blanked stamp; remaining system blocks are joined with a blank line instead of glued together.
* **Calculator:** `log2(2^k)` was off in the last digit for 9 of the 62 powers of two (e.g. `log2(2^29) = 29.000000000000004`), and `round(0.49999999999999994)` returned 1. Both fixed and checked with real Java runs of the same algorithms; tests added.
* Chat: "Thinking..." before the first token is now "Reading..." (earlier change).
* Context footer "0 / n_ctx" and the KV wipe after an accepted-EOG draft: see `docs/CTX_AND_KV_REUSE.md` (patch 0005).

Looked at and found fine: engine `.cpp` warnings (one unused parameter in `router_hook.cpp`, pre-existing), `Workspace.resolve` (canonical path + root prefix check), `GgufInspector` bounds, `ContextPlanner` budget arithmetic, division sites with possible zero denominators, catch-all handlers around suspend calls (only three in `FileViewModel`, inside `viewModelScope`, harmless).
Known and left alone: the token estimate is `bytes / 3` (conservative; it overestimates English by roughly a quarter); Qwen-style templates drop old reasoning when a new user turn starts, so part of the KV prefix cannot be reused on those models.

Historical note: the baseline assumptions below were first cross-checked against upstream `examples/android` (v0.24.0). The current app vendors the BigMoeOnEdge 0.28.0 core with local patches; use the current no-copy workflow and release/status notes for the v0.4.0 behavior.
Baseline behavior and storage notes:
* Models must be on a real filesystem path: the engine streams experts with `O_DIRECT`. In-app copies land in
  `filesDir/models` (f2fs/ext4). Files read from emulated external storage fall back to buffered I/O.
* Upstream picks the first shard of split models (`-00001-of-0000N.gguf`); siblings are found next to it.
  The model list here hides shards other than the first.
* Upstream defaults: 4 I/O lanes, 4 compute threads, dense weights = anon, expert cache 2000 MiB fixed (auto is
  optional). This app's defaults: auto cache with a 1536 MB RAM floor, 4/4, anon.
* Some models (e.g. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) need *Pinned* dense weights and a small cache (1000–1500 MiB on 12 GB).

Flow: Models screen → **Add GGUF from storage (no copy)** to register a GGUF already in shared Internal storage,
or **Import GGUF file(s) (copy)** to copy a selected file into app-private storage with progress, cancellation,
and free-space checks, or `adb push` into the folder shown on screen → "Load" → pre-flight (GGUF magic, RAM < 6 GB
warning, cache > 60 % RAM warning, Pinned warning) → confirm → `Session::open` on the IO dispatcher. The engine
reports no progress, so the UI shows an indeterminate bar. The last loaded path is persisted; "load on app start"
is optional (off by default).
Load-time settings (context, sampling, threads, cache, dense weights) are fixed by `Session::open`. Settings
shows "needs reload" and the Models screen offers "Reload".
Heuristic thresholds (6 GB RAM, 60 %) are this project's, not upstream requirements.

The default **Add GGUF from storage (no copy)** action opens Android's document picker. When the selected item comes from Android's External Storage DocumentsProvider, the app resolves it to its real filesystem path, validates the GGUF header, and registers it without copying. Browse to **Internal storage** in the picker for files in the phone's shared storage. Some cloud/Downloads/provider URIs do not expose a real path; use **Import GGUF file(s) (copy)** for those. An **Advanced: enter a path manually** section remains available for troubleshooting.
On Android 11 and newer, Android generally blocks arbitrary shared-storage paths until the user explicitly grants this app **Allow access to manage all files** in the system settings page. The no-copy flow opens that settings page only when needed and retries registration after returning. If the user does not grant access, Import remains available and copies the selected file into app-private storage.

The app declares `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE` solely to support this opt-in large-file/no-copy workflow. This is a restricted Android permission and may not be accepted for distribution through Google Play; distribution channels must comply with Google's current all-files-access policy. Direct reads from emulated/shared storage can also fall back to buffered I/O, so permission enables access but does not guarantee the same I/O performance as app-private storage.
The app now has a complete source-level image/video attachment pipeline and a native `mtmd` integration path.

* `AttachmentManager` copies selected media into the private workspace under `uploads/`.
* Images are decoded to RGB, EXIF-rotated, downscaled, and passed as `ImageData`.
* Videos are sampled into RGB frames with the configured frame count; native `MTMD_VIDEO` support is intentionally OFF,
  so ffmpeg is not a dependency of the Android build.
* Image/video menu items are disabled unless the currently loaded model has a projector.

* `ModelManager` treats `*mmproj*.gguf` as projector files rather than normal text models.
* The Models load dialog offers a projector dropdown and suggests a matching projector by normalized model name.
* The selected projector is persisted as `lastMmprojPath` and restored by auto-load/reload.
* Status shows `Vision: active` when a projector is loaded.

`SessionConfig::mmproj_path`, `GenerateRequest::images`, JNI byte-array transport, and the `BMOE_ENABLE_MULTIMODAL`
build flag are implemented. When `BMOE_HAVE_MTMD` is present, `Session` creates an mtmd context, inserts one default
media marker per image, tokenizes text+images through `mtmd_tokenize`, and pre-fills through
`mtmd_helper_eval_chunks`.
Image turns explicitly disable speculative decoding because the text-only KV mirror cannot represent image embeddings.
The image turn starts from a clean KV and marks the cache as containing media. A later turn therefore clears/replays text
history instead of pretending the old image embeddings are reusable.

* `session.cpp` passes host syntax with `BMOE_HAVE_MTMD=1` and without it.
* `native-bridge.cpp` passes host syntax with a minimal JNI stub and mtmd enabled.
* The Android CMake/NDK link, a real vision model, a matching mmproj, image inference, video frame inference, and device
  memory/performance are **not verified in this sandbox**.
The remaining risk is therefore integration/runtime rather than an intentionally omitted feature.

h: Hexagon HTP prompt-prefill build for Android
t: The ordinary CPU APK is unchanged and stays CPU-only. The optional NPU workflow builds the app's vendored `ggml-hexagon` backend and HTP DSP skeletons from the same source revision as `libonedge-engine.so`. A Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 provides a Hexagon HTP generation compatible with the v73 skeleton target, but hardware family alone is not proof that the runtime and model graph are compatible.

Run `.github/workflows/android-npu.yml` with **workflow_dispatch**. The workflow checks free disk before starting; caps native and Gradle build parallelism at two workers; deletes the native build tree and toolchain Docker image after staging; and verifies both the staged files and files extracted back out of the APK. The ordinary `.github/workflows/build.yml` is not modified.

The native configure command must supply `-DBMOE_ENABLE_HEXAGON=ON`, the actual `HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT`/`HEXAGON_TOOLS_ROOT`, and `-DPREBUILT_LIB_DIR=android_aarch64`. This snapshot has a CMake include of `${HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT}/build/cmake/hexagon_fun.cmake`; that helper belongs to the external SDK image rather than this source archive. A known failure mode for this SDK helper is a missing/empty `PREBUILT_LIB_DIR`; however, this source archive already supplied the outer `android_aarch64` selector before this patch. The exact `hexagon_fun.cmake` traceback is not attached, and the nested HTP CMake build also passes its own `toolv19_vNN` selector. This patch adds validation and forces a clean build tree to rule out stale CMake cache/artifacts, but it does not claim the specific error is fixed until a real toolchain workflow successfully configures and builds.

The build intentionally stages only these Android ARM64 ABI libraries in `app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a/`:
- `libonedge-engine.so`
- `libc++_shared.so`
The DSP-side skeleton ELF files are **not** Android ARM64 JNI libraries. They are staged as APK assets under `app/src/main/assets/hexagon/`:
- `libggml-htp-v73.so`
- `libggml-htp-v75.so`
- `libggml-htp-v79.so`
- `libggml-htp-v81.so`
Before the native engine is loaded, `HexagonRuntimeSetup` extracts the four files to the app-private `files/hexagon-dsp` directory and prepends that directory to `ADSP_LIBRARY_PATH`, preserving pre-existing paths. On a CPU-only APK, the asset bundle is absent and startup setup safely no-ops.

- **Unavailable**: either the native engine lacks `BMOE_HAVE_HEXAGON`, HTP0 is not registered, or HTP0 cannot open its FastRPC/DSP session. The UI shows the reason reported by native code.
- **Available**: a real `ggml_backend_dev_init(HTP0)` probe succeeded. This proves the backend can open a runtime session, not that a model graph has executed on it.
- **Enabled/ready for a loaded model**: the requested HTP prefill path survived `Session::open`; a failed/missing device makes model loading fail instead of silently clearing the device and continuing on CPU.
- **Execution evidence**: after a generation, logcat reports `NPU prefill evidence: device_tokens=... device_nodes=...`. `device_nodes > 0` is the source's explicit count of graph nodes actually computed by the device backend for that prompt. Zero is not proof of execution. Short or reused prompts can legitimately report zero.

The custom prefill path captures layer weights, moves eligible weights to device buffers, reserves a prefill graph on HTP for chunks wider than `min_tokens`, and rebinds to host state for CPU token-by-token decode. The vendored ggml Hexagon backend advertises only its implemented operation set; model shape/type/backend capability checks determine which actual graph nodes can execute there. A successful probe or bundled file cannot guarantee every model offloads or improves in speed.

```bash
bash scripts/validate-npu-source.sh
bash scripts/verify-npu-payload.sh app/src/main/jniLibs/arm64-v8a app/src/main/assets/hexagon
```
The payload command requires the real staged ELF files. It checks ARM64 architecture for the Android JNI engine/runtime, Hexagon architecture for DSP skeletons, the NPU-specific native status marker, and SHA-256 values. CI re-extracts the payload from the resulting APK and runs the same verifier against the extracted files.

h: Verification boundary for this source patch
t: The source/static checks do not compile the Hexagon engine, create an APK, or prove physical-device runtime behavior. This environment has host CMake/Ninja, but no Android SDK/NDK, no Qualcomm Hexagon SDK/toolchain image available locally, and no attached Android device. The Gradle wrapper failed before Gradle startup because `services.gradle.org` could not be resolved. Therefore no APK or device benchmark is claimed as built here. A successful workflow and nonzero device-node telemetry remain required before claiming NPU execution.

* `SessionConfig::chatml = true` makes `Session` own the conversation: it keeps `chat_history`, renders the
  model's own chat template over the WHOLE history every turn (`common_chat_templates_apply`) and reuses the
  common KV prefix. `GenerateRequest::prompt` is therefore **only the newest user message**.
* Upstream `Session` has no system prompt and no way to load earlier turns. `clear_kv = true` empties the
  history; `clear_kv = false` continues the engine's own history.
* A cancelled `generate()` rolls the whole turn back (KV and the pushed user message).
Because of that the old `AgentController` (raw `"system\nUser: x\nAssistant:"` string) was wrong twice:
the template was applied on top of a hand-made template, and the history was never restored.

`GenerateRequest` gains `system_prompt` and `history` (`ChatTurn{role,content}`), honoured only in chat mode on a
`clear_kv = true` request: the fresh conversation is seeded with `system` + `history`, then `prompt` is appended
as the newest user turn, and the normal prefill covers all of it. Also: `n_predict <= 0` = fill the remaining
context ("unlimited"), a failed n_ctx check no longer leaves the pushed user message in `chat_history`, and a
failed `seq_rm` rollback no longer leaves `kv_tokens` claiming a valid prefix.
Callers that set none of the new fields get upstream behaviour.

`EngineController` remembers a **state key** for what the engine currently holds:
`stateKey(sessionId, id of last message the engine has seen, hash(system prompt))`.
| situation | key matches? | call |
|---|---|---|
| next message in the open chat | yes | `clear_kv=false`, prompt only (KV reused) |
| tool result follow-up | yes (key of the assistant message) | `clear_kv=false`, prompt = `<tool_response>…` |
| open another chat / History | no | `clear_kv=true` + system + saved history replay |
| app restart, model reload | no (key reset) | replay |
| turn was stopped / failed | no | replay (partial assistant text is saved, engine rolled back) |
| system prompt or tool set changed | no (hash differs) | replay |
| deleted/edited message | no | replay |

`ContextPlanner.prepare` normalises the replay (drops empty turns, merges same-role neighbours, folds a trailing
unanswered user turn into the prompt, drops the oldest whole pairs to fit `historyBudget`). If the engine still
answers "exceeds n_ctx" the controller retries up to twice with half the history. "Unlimited" answers reserve a
quarter of the context.
Only the engine's `Finished` event commits a key, and only after the assistant message is saved
(`AgentController` calls `commitState`). A crash between the two just causes one extra replay.

There is no regenerate button (not requested). Nothing prevents adding one later: delete the last assistant
message → the key no longer matches → replay.

h: ASSUMPTIONS (need a real model to confirm)
t:
* The template renders the replayed history the same way it rendered the live turns (true for standard Jinja
  templates; tool-call text is stored as plain assistant text, which is what the model produced).
* Reasoning text is not replayed (the engine keeps it out of `chat_history`).

A replay costs a prefill of everything the context does not hold. `Session::save_kv(prefix)` writes what it holds
(state + tokens, draft context, speculative state, context checkpoints), `load_kv(prefix)` puts it back and ends the
engine-held conversation; the app then replays as in the table above and the prefix reuse keeps what matches. So the
table's "replay" rows for *another chat*, *app restart* and *model reload* become "load snapshot, then replay".
* `EngineController` tracks `kvSessionId` (the chat the context holds), `kvDirty` and `kvFingerprint` (model file name,
  size, first MiB + KV type, LoRA, draft setup). `swapSnapshot(target)` runs before the first replay of a turn for a
  chat other than `kvSessionId`: save the held chat (if dirty and >= 512 tokens), load the target's snapshot if any.
* Also saved in `loadModel` / `unload` (before the old session goes) and from `MainActivity.onStop`
  (`saveSnapshotNow`, skipped while generating).

* Only chat turns (`expectedKey` contains `|`) own a snapshot. Helper turns, `decide()` and API requests set
  `kvSessionId = null` and write nothing; the next chat turn loads the chat's last snapshot.
* A wrong or stale snapshot costs time, not correctness: reuse is token by token. A snapshot from another model of the
  same shape would be wrong, hence the fingerprint. The engine refuses a state that does not fit (KV type, layers,
  draft setup, more tokens than n_ctx) and leaves the context empty.
* Not saved: a context that holds an image (`kv_has_media`).

h: Web search modes (Settings → Web and image search; globe button in the chat)
t:
The globe toggle is **off by default**. The `ALWAYS` mode below only applies after the user enables the globe.
* **Every message (default mode, `ALWAYS`)**: the loaded model first creates a short, hidden search query from the
  user's request and recent conversation context. The app searches that generated query, stores the results as a
  `TOOL` message, then runs the normal answer generation with `message + <tool_response>…`. If query generation
  fails or returns nothing, it safely falls back to a normalized version of the user's message. This adds one short
  model generation before each automatic search, but avoids blindly searching the raw message wording.
* **Only when the model asks (`AUTO`)**: the tool protocol below; small models often never call the tool.
* Provider order: Brave (if a key is set) → SearXNG (if an https URL is set) → **DuckDuckGo HTML (no account)**
  → Wikipedia search API. The DuckDuckGo path scrapes `html.duckduckgo.com/html/`; it can be rate-limited or
  change shape, which is why Wikipedia is the fallback and a failure is reported to the model as text.

h: Web search modes (Settings → Web and image search; globe button in the chat)
t: * The UI shows "Searching the web for “…”", then a collapsible "Tool result" card with the sources. When Web Search is enabled, the model can also call `image_search`; this uses Wikimedia Commons, displays thumbnail cards in chat, and includes a source page plus available license/creator metadata. The image tool remains unavailable while the globe/Web Search toggle is off.

h: Protocol (prompt plus an optional lazy grammar, see below)
t:
System prompt (when "web search" is on) lists the tools and asks for exactly
`<tool_call>{"name": "...", "arguments": {...}}</tool_call>`. The app answers with a user turn
`<tool_response>
[tool]
result
</tool_response>`.

* `StreamOutputParser` hides tool-call blocks while streaming, including tags split across tokens.
* `ToolProtocol.parseCall` accepts code fences, surrounding prose, trailing commas, smart quotes, single quotes,
  `parameters`/`args` aliases, arguments encoded as a JSON string, and a truncated object.
* Invalid call → visible notice + a corrective `<tool_response>` telling the model to retry (`malformedFeedback`).
* At most 3 tool rounds and 3 calls per round; then a visible "limit reached" message.
* Tool errors, timeouts (20 s) and oversized results (6000 chars) are returned to the model as text; the app never
  throws because of a tool.
* Stop button ends the loop even while a tool is running.

Settings → Tools → Agent → "Grammar-checked tool calls" (on by default). `parser/ToolGrammar` builds a GBNF grammar for
`<tool_call>{"name": <one of the enabled tools>, "arguments": {<JSON object>}}</tool_call>` (up to 4 calls, whitespace
between, then only end-of-turn). `AgentController` sends it with every round as `GenerationRequest.toolGrammar`;
it reaches the engine as `GenerateRequest::tool_grammar` / `tool_grammar_trigger` (JNI `nativeGenerate`).
Engine side (`core/src/engine/tool_grammar.{h,cpp}`, `session.cpp`):
* A LAZY grammar (`llama_sampler_init_grammar_lazy_patterns`): free sampling until the output contains `<tool_call>`,
  then every token must continue the grammar. Prose before a call is unaffected.
* It wraps whatever the turn draws from (session chain, per-request chain, or argmax). Fast path: take the token the
  turn would take, check that single token against the grammar, and only on rejection resample with the grammar
  applied to the whole vocabulary.

* Speculative decoding: while the grammar is active, drafts are verified by drawing through it instead of argmax, so
  the grammar sees every emitted token in order; the draw that rejects a draft becomes the next token directly.
* Never accepts a token the grammar rejects or an end-of-generation inside an open call (llama.cpp aborts on both);
  a dead end ends the turn instead and the tolerant parser + retry take over.
* Skipped when the turn may reason first (`think` on, or `ThinkControl::None`): a `<tool_call>` mentioned inside a
  reasoning span would switch it on there. With "Think after tool results" off (default) this means every round
  after the first is constrained, and all rounds when Thinking is off.
* A grammar that does not parse is dropped with a log line; the turn runs unconstrained.
* The stateless API-server path is unchanged.

Tested on the host against the vendored llama.cpp with a vocab-only GGUF: valid call untouched, unknown tool name
overruled, end-of-turn refused mid-call, prose after a call refused, raw newline inside a JSON string refused, trigger
split over single-character tokens, 60,000 characters of prose before a call (about 0.5 ms per token on a desktop CPU
for the trigger search). Not yet run on a device.

The tool system is intentionally registry-driven. A tool implements `com.bigmoe.onedge.tools.Tool` with:
* `name`: stable machine-readable tool name.
* `description`: concise model-facing capability text.
* `parametersSchema`: JSON Schema-style object describing arguments and required fields.
* `category`: `FILES`, `CODE`, `WEB` or `UTILITIES` for UI/settings grouping.
* `describe(arguments)`: short live UI label while the tool runs.
* `confirmation(arguments)`: optional approval request. Return a `ConfirmationRequest` for edits, replacements,
  deletes, or other destructive actions; return `null` for safe operations.
* `execute(arguments, ctx)`: the real operation. `ToolContext` identifies the chat/session so created artifacts can be linked.
Register the tool in `AppContainer.toolManager`. `ToolManager` then supplies it to the prompt, parses its calls, runs it
off the main thread with a timeout/result-size cap, emits a tool-running event, and routes confirmation through the chat UI.

For a switchable tool, add its name to the appropriate `*_TOOL_NAMES` set in `AgentController` and expose the setting in
`EngineSettings`/Settings UI. For file-producing tools, update `ArtifactRegistry` so the chat's artifact list stays in sync.
Current groups:
* Files: list/read/search/create/edit/rename/delete/create_folder/create_project/export_zip. `create_folder` also lists the folder in the chat's files.
* Code: search_code/analyze_code/run_javascript.
* Utilities: get_datetime/calculate/convert_units/random_number/device_info (offline, read-only; `UTILITY_TOOL_NAMES`).
* Web: web_search/read_webpage/extract_webpage/image_search. `image_search` queries Wikimedia Commons and returns thumbnails with source URLs and available attribution/license metadata. It is enabled by the same opt-in globe/Web Search control and is off on a new install.
Security rules are deliberate: every file path is resolved inside the private workspace, destructive changes require user
approval, JavaScript runs in an offline WebView sandbox with no JS bridge, and artifact HTML uses a restrictive CSP.

Tool access: Settings -> Tool access and the chat's wrench menu hold the same three switches (Files, Code, Utilities); the
web tools follow the globe button. The model uses an enabled tool on its own when it decides it needs one.

BigMoeOnEdge² can work as an **agent**: the local model does not only answer in text, it runs real commands on the
device, reads their results and keeps going until the task is done. Typical jobs:
* turn a text file into an audiobook (it installs a TTS package, writes a Python script, runs it, checks the MP3),
* convert or cut audio/video with ffmpeg, resize pictures, draw a small cover image with Pillow,
* unpack, search, rename or sort files, build a ZIP,
* write a Python script, run it, read the error, fix it and run it again.
The commands run in the separately installed [Termux](https://github.com/termux/termux-app) app. BigMoeOnEdge² itself
cannot run programs (Android 10+ forbids executing files from an app's own data folder), so it hands each command to
Termux through Termux's official `RUN_COMMAND` interface and waits for the answer. Without Termux the app works as
before; the Termux switch then simply has nothing to use.
---

Settings → **Tools, web search, pictures & videos → Tools → Termux** shows a status line for every step and copies the
commands below with one tap.
1. **Install Termux** from [F-Droid](https://f-droid.org/packages/com.termux/) or
   [GitHub](https://github.com/termux/termux-app/releases) – *not* from Google Play (that build is outdated and lacks
   the interface). Open it once so it finishes its first start.
2. **In Termux**, run:
   ```bash
   termux-setup-storage
   mkdir -p ~/.termux && echo 'allow-external-apps = true' >> ~/.termux/termux.properties && termux-reload-settings
   ```
   The first line gives Termux access to shared storage (and so to the workspace); the second allows other apps – this
   one – to send commands. Optional: `ln -s ~/storage/shared/BigMoe/workspace ~/bigmoe` makes the workspace reachable
   as `~/bigmoe` when you work in Termux yourself.

3. **Shared workspace:** Settings → **Diagnostics & workspace → Shared workspace folder** → on, and allow
   *All files access* when Android asks. The workspace moves to `Internal storage/BigMoe/workspace`, a folder Termux can
   see. Existing files are moved along; a `.nomedia` file keeps generated pictures and audio out of the gallery and
   music apps. (Turning the switch off moves everything back to private app storage.)
4. **Permission:** Settings → Tools → Termux → **Grant permission** (*Run commands in Termux environment*). If no
   dialog appears: App settings → Permissions → Additional permissions. If the entry is missing there, Termux was
   installed after BigMoeOnEdge²; installing the next update of this app makes Android offer it.
5. **Test Termux:** the button runs a tiny command and shows Termux's answer: `Termux answers from: <workspace path>`,
   the CPU architecture and the Python version (or a note that Python is not installed yet – the agent installs it
   itself when it needs it).

6. Turn on the **Termux** switch (Settings → Tools → Termux, or the tool chips above the chat input).
All four status lines – *Termux installed*, *Permission to run commands*, *Workspace in the shared folder* and the
test – should be green.
---

```
you ──► model ──► <tool_call> run_shell {"command": "..."} ──► BigMoeOnEdge² ──RUN_COMMAND──► Termux (bash)
                                                                    ▲                              │
                         model reads exit code + output ◄───────────┴──── stdout, stderr, exit ◄───┘
```
* When Termux is enabled, the model gets the tool **`run_shell`** (`command`, optional `cwd` inside the workspace,
  optional `timeout_seconds` 5–1800, default 120) plus a short instruction: use the shell **on its own**, without asking
  first and without telling you to run commands; work in steps; **check before installing** (e.g.
  `command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || pkg install -y ffmpeg`, `python3 -c 'import gtts' 2>/dev/null || pip install gtts`);
  run `pkg update -y` if `pkg` fails; never start interactive programs; only report success when the exit code and the
  output show it, and name the files it made.

* Every command runs with **the workspace as the current folder**. A file the model writes with `create_file` and a
  file a Python script produces are the same files; you see them in the Workspace screen and can open, share or
  download them there.
* The app wraps the command in a small bash script that records the process id and copies the output to a log file in
  the hidden folder `.bigmoe/` inside the workspace. That is how the chat can show the latest output line live and how
  a command can be stopped. The files are removed when the command ends; `.bigmoe` is not shown in the Workspace
  screen.
* The model sees `exit code: N` and the stdout/stderr (Termux keeps the last ~100 KB of each stream; a cut is marked).
  If a command fails, the model reads the error and tries a fix in the next step.

One answer may contain several tool rounds: install → write script → run → check → fix → run again. Settings → Tools
→ **Agent → Agent steps per answer** sets the limit: 6, 12, **20 (default)**, 30 or 50 rounds. When the limit is
reached the agent stops and says so; write "continue" to let it go on.
When the context is nearly full, the agent stops *before* the next step instead of running into a cut-off answer, and
tells you. Start a new chat, or raise the context size on the Models / Engine settings and reload.
---

h: 3. What you see in the chat
t:
* **Live status row** above the input while a tool runs: what it is doing (`Termux: pip install gtts…`), the elapsed
  time with the limit (`1 min 05 s / 10 min`), and "no output for N min" when a command has been silent for a while.
  While the model is writing a tool call you already see `Writing run_shell: python3 make_audio.py…`; after a command it
  shows *Reading the result…*.
* **Output, folded:** under the status row, `▸ Output` with the latest line. Tap it to unfold the command's whole output
  so far; it follows the end like a terminal. Python output appears as it is printed.
* **Cancel** next to the running command shows *Stopping…* at once, stops the command **including all child processes**
  (TERM, then KILL for the whole process tree). Only that call is cancelled: the model gets an error and decides how
  to go on. The **Stop** button ends the whole run.

h: 3. What you see in the chat
t:
* **Time limits:** if a command takes longer than its `timeout_seconds`, it is stopped the same way and the model gets
  the output so far with a note. The tool description tells the model to ask for a longer limit for installs (up to
  1800 s = 30 minutes).
* **When Termux does not react:** if Termux has not started a command after 20 s (Android paused it in the background),
  the agent gets a clear error instead of waiting for the limit, and the command is marked so it can never start later.
  If a command finished but Termux's answer got lost, the app reads the exit code and output from the files after 5 s.
* **No hanging on prompts:** commands get no input, so a program that asks a question fails at once with an error the
  model can react to (e.g. by adding `-y`).
* **Results** appear as collapsible tool cards titled `Termux · exit 0 ✓`, `Termux · exit 1 ✗`,
  `Termux · cancelled` or `Termux · stopped (time limit)`; tap one to see the full command output.
---

Settings → Tools → **Agent → Approval**:
* **Ask before changes and commands (default):** every Termux command opens a dialog showing the exact command and the
  folder. File edits and deletes ask as well.
* **Allow everything without asking:** commands, edits and deletes run without a dialog. Convenient for a task you are
  watching; the agent can then work through many steps alone.
Keep in mind:
* A command runs with **all of Termux's rights**: it can change or delete files in Termux's home and in shared storage
  (all-files access is on for the shared workspace) and it can use the network.
* Text the model reads – web pages, downloaded files, documents you attach – can contain instructions it might follow
  ("prompt injection"). With *Allow everything*, do not let it work on untrusted content unattended.
* The workspace path is the only place the app *sends* commands to, but a command itself can `cd` anywhere Termux can
  go. The approval dialog is the real safeguard.
---

Settings → Tools → Agent → **Grammar-checked tool calls** (on by default). As soon as the model writes `<tool_call>`,
the engine only allows tokens that continue a **valid call to an enabled tool** (correct name, valid JSON). Small and
heavily quantised models then no longer fail on broken JSON or invented tool names. Details:
* It is not applied on turns where the model reasons first (Thinking on, or a model that always thinks), because the
  grammar would also constrain the reasoning.
* While it is active, *Guess ahead* (MTP / n-gram) drafts are checked against the grammar as well, so speculative
  decoding keeps working.
* If a model behaves oddly with it, switch it off; calls are then parsed from free text as before.
More in [`docs/tool-calling.md`](../tool-calling.md).
---

* **Tool use is the hard part**, not speed alone. Models trained for agentic tool calls work best; in practice
  Qwen3.5/3.6 (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) and Gemma 4 are reliable choices. Very small models (≤ 4B) often lose track over
  many steps.
* **Thinking off** for agent work is usually faster and lets the tool grammar apply; turn it on for tasks that need
  planning.
* **Context:** each round adds the command and its output to the context. 16k fills up after a few long outputs; 24–32k
  is more comfortable if RAM allows.
* **KV cache per model (Models page → model card → KV cache):** `Q8_0` roughly halves the KV cache memory with almost no
  quality loss – the easiest way to afford a bigger context. `Q4_0` saves more but costs quality. F16 is the default.
  A type the device cannot use for that model falls back to F16 at load, with a note.
* **Expert cache:** for MoE models streamed from flash, a smaller expert cache leaves RAM for the KV cache and for
  Termux's own processes (Python, ffmpeg). If Android starts killing other apps during long runs, lower it a bit.
---

> Make an audiobook from `story.txt` in German, one MP3 per chapter.
The agent checks for Python and a TTS package, installs what is missing, writes `make_audiobook.py`, runs it, lists the
MP3 files with their sizes and tells you where they are.
> Draw a 128×128 cover for the audiobook: dark blue, a book and the title "Der Sturm".
It checks for Pillow (`python3 -c 'import PIL'`), installs it if needed, writes and runs a small drawing script and
reports `cover.png`.
> Cut the first 30 seconds of `talk.mp4` and save the audio as `intro.m4a`.
`command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || pkg install -y ffmpeg`, then one ffmpeg call, then `ls -la intro.m4a` to check.

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| *Termux is not installed* although it is | It must be the F-Droid/GitHub build (`com.termux`). Reinstall this app's update once after installing Termux. |
| *Termux could not run the command … allow-external-apps* | Run the `allow-external-apps` line from step 2 in Termux, then `termux-reload-settings`. |
| *may not run commands in Termux yet* | Grant *Run commands in Termux environment* (step 4). |
| *the workspace is in the app's private storage* | Turn on *Shared workspace folder* (step 3). |
| `Permission denied` on files in the workspace | Run `termux-setup-storage` in Termux and allow storage access. |
| `pkg install` fails / *unable to locate package* | Let it run `pkg update -y` first; on a slow mirror run `termux-change-repo` once in Termux. |
| A command hangs | Tap **Cancel** next to it; the whole process tree is stopped and the model tries another way. Unfold *Output* to see where it stopped. |
| The agent explains commands instead of running them | Make sure the Termux switch is on for this chat (tool chips above the input). |
| The agent stops with a context note | Start a new chat, or raise the context size and use a `Q8_0` KV cache. |
| *Termux did not start the command within 20s* | Android paused Termux. Open Termux once and allow it to run in the background (battery settings: no restrictions / allow background activity). |

BigMoeOnEdge² runs large GGUF models (including Mixture-of-Experts models bigger than the phone's RAM) locally on
Android, with chat, tools, a workspace, a local API server and – new – an agent that runs real commands through Termux.

* **[Agent mode with Termux](Agent-mode-with-Termux)** – setup, how the agent works, live status and cancel, approval
  and safety, grammar-checked tool calls, model and KV cache tips, examples and troubleshooting.

* [README](https://github.com/int3ks/BigMoeOnEdge-Snap#readme) – overview, download, building
* [Releases](https://github.com/int3ks/BigMoeOnEdge-Snap/releases/latest) – the latest APK
* [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/int3ks/BigMoeOnEdge-Snap/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) – every change of the Snap fork
> The pages in this wiki are also kept in the repository under [`docs/wiki/`](https://github.com/int3ks/BigMoeOnEdge-Snap/tree/main/docs/wiki).

- **Wiki import, fixed folder:** the wiki is always `<internal storage>/BigMoe/wiki` (never the app's own storage); without all-files access Settings shows "Allow access to all files" and the wiki stays empty. "Import files" (Settings → Tools → Wiki) copies picked `.md`/`.markdown`/`.txt` files in (same name = replaced) and unpacks a `.zip` (a Notion export) into a subfolder named after it, emptied first, with only its text files and their folders (no paths outside it); the rest is skipped and counted.

- **Wiki tool (`wiki_search`)**: own knowledge from `.md`/`.txt` files in `<internal storage>/BigMoe/wiki` (without all-files access: the app's external files folder; subfolders included). Switch in Settings → Tools (shows folder, file and passage count, "Read the folder again") and in the chat's tools menu, per chat. `tools/WikiTool.kt`: chunks like the help index, an inverted BM25 index with only offsets kept (chunk text is read from the file for the hits), rebuilt when a file changes, dropped after 10 min without a search. The model is told to search with German and English keywords and to try it before a web search. **Search for both Help and Wiki**: words are any letters now (umlauts were split before), and longer words starting with a query word count half (German compounds: "akku" finds "akkuverbrauch").

- **Help tool (`app_help`)**: Settings → Tools → Help (also in the chat's tools menu) lets the model look up how this app and its engine work, offline. `scripts/build-help-index.py` cuts `docs/*.md`, `docs/wiki`, this change log and the longer settings texts into about 330 chunks (`assets/help/help.json`, 204 KiB); `tools/HelpTool.kt` searches them with BM25 and returns the best four. The tool description tells the model to search with 2 to 6 English keywords (the sources are English) and to answer in the user's language; the result ends with the same reminder, and a miss asks for other English keywords. With the switch on, the system prompt also asks the model to call it before answering questions about the app.

- **Chat and model UI polish (phone):** Copy and Read aloud under an answer are icon-only; the run statistics sit in one ellipsized line and unfold on a tap; a tap on the chat title unfolds title and model line. **Model display name (alias):** the pencil on a model card no longer renames the file but sets a display name (`.model-aliases.properties`, `core/ModelAliases.kt`), used in the model list, the chat header and the variant bar; empty = file name. **Settings advice:** every suggested change has its own Apply button (ticked afterwards), "Apply all" takes the open ones.
- **Fix: the translation list missed the page's texts.** A page change emptied the list in an effect, which runs after the new page has composed its texts, so a page that did not recompose showed nothing. Texts now carry when they were asked for, and the list keeps those from shortly before the page change on.

- **Translation mode** (Settings → Language): while on, `t()` notes the texts of the current page and a translate button (bottom left) lists them with their current translation. Tapping one asks a local model for the translation (no model loaded: pick one, it is loaded first, as for the performance log's advice); the result can be edited and "Apply" writes it into the language file in use (`I18n.putTranslation`; with none, a template for the device language is made first) and shows it at once.
- **Cleanup:** the per-token Metrics CSV is gone from the app (setting, share button, file path; the performance log covers what it was used for, the engine's CSV sink stays for the CLI); the old Auto ceiling setting and the dead CACHE_AUTO_MB branches of the device tuner are gone; 25 outdated docs (BigMoeOnEdge+ handoff, 0.5.x notes, old audits, copied upstream sources) moved to `docs/archive/`.

- **Language: "Share … for translation"** sends the chosen (or the system language's) JSON file with a prompt to Gemini or any app: translate the values, keep keys and placeholders, answer with the whole file.

- **App language from JSON files** (`core/I18n.kt`): Settings → Appearance → Language offers System and every `*.json` in `<internal storage>/BigMoe/language` (without all-files access: the app's external files folder). A file is `{"name", "lang", "strings": {English: translation}}`; the English text in the code is the key, a missing file or entry shows English, `{0}`… take filled-in values. System picks the file whose `lang` is the device language. "Create a template for <language>" (shown when the device language is not English and has no file) writes every known text with its English value. Texts reach the translation through `t("…")` or the settings helpers (Hint, Section, SwitchRow, ChoiceSetting with its options, group and foldout titles) and the top bar; `scripts/extract-strings.py` collects them into `assets/language/english.json` (358 so far). The rest of the app follows screen by screen.
- **Narrow screens:** with less than 600 dp width (a phone upright) Settings, Hugging Face and Log sit in a ⋮ menu of the top bar.

- **Row-gathered tables no longer locked by NPU prefill:** the switch stays usable; a load with the NPU on for the model (global or its card) leaves row streaming out instead of failing.
- **Auto cache: no maximum.** The setting is gone from the UI; free RAM, the reserve and the app's swap are the limit (the engine clamps to the full expert set).

With a prefill device the prefill now stops only at the end of the preamble and 4 tokens before the prompt's end (`Stops::device`). - **Fix: a second Regenerate prefilled the whole conversation again** on hybrid models (Qwen3.5/3.6) and after a KV snapshot (MagicPad, 7.04: 12 of 576 tokens reused). When the checkpoint list was full, the eviction rule from upstream #603 dropped every checkpoint an earlier request took within `checkpoint_min_step` (8192) of the one before it, so with 4 kept everything but the preamble's went, including the one 4 tokens before the prompt's end. Now only the coldest share of the cache (by last use) is ever offered, and a drop never takes the budget below the rest; the cache brake can still go lower. 100 % = upstream's rule.

- **Sliding-window layers keep only their window in the KV cache** (upstream #580, `swa_full` off): llama.cpp's default gave Gemma's SWA layers a cache as long as the context; now they hold the window plus one ubatch (Gemma 4 26B-A4B at 16k context: context memory about 2.3 GiB → 0.4 GiB upstream; checkpoints copy only the window, so they shrink too). A cut further back than the window (Regenerate or an edit after a long answer) is caught by the sliding-window check added on 2026-11-20 and served from a context checkpoint (now also 4 tokens before each prompt's end) or a full prefill. KV snapshots saved by an older build with the full SWA cache do not fit and are refused; the chat is then replayed as usual. - **Engine fixes and speed-ups from upstream BigMoeOnEdge (0.41–0.46), ported onto the 0.28-based engine:**

- **A failed expert read ends the run on the serial path too** (#668). Without overlap (the default) a failed read (storage error, a shard cut short, a drive removed) was dropped by the caller: the entry counted as resident, the matmul ran on a slice nobody had read, the answer looked like a success and the entry was served as a hit later. Now the turn fails with "expert stream I/O failed during prefill/decode", and a failed row gather ends it the same way.

- **Context checkpoints where llama.cpp's server takes them** (#603): at the start of a user message (found from the template's own message delimiters, the first one = end of the system prompt) and 4 and n_ubatch + 4 tokens before the prompt's end; the prefill stops there. On hybrid / sliding-window models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Gemma, ...) a follow-up or Regenerate reuses almost the whole conversation instead of falling back to the previous prompt's end (upstream: 15.9 s → 3.5 s for a follow-up after a 7k prompt; a new chat with the same 4.4k system prompt 17.5 s → 0.9 s). The preamble's checkpoint is evicted last. Host test: Regenerate now reuses 74 of 78 tokens instead of 33.

- **Expert cache evicts by decayed frequency** (#505, half-life 8 tokens, `MoeStreamConfig::cache_freq_half_life`, 0 = old LRU): below one token's working set LRU hit 0 %; upstream measured 0 → 27 % hits and 6.1 → 8.5 tok/s with a small cache on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 4–5 % fewer bytes read with a large one. **A prompt's misses enter cold** (`cache_prefill_cold`): a long prompt prefilled on the CPU no longer flushes what decode reuses. **The NPU prefill copies experts the cache holds from RAM** instead of reading them from flash (`PrefillDeviceConfig::from_cache`). Lossless: only what stays in RAM changes.

- **The expert cache no longer pushes Android into swap** (#528, #530, #554; `cache_discard`, on): an entry no layer used in the last pass is offered to the kernel with `MADV_FREE`, which drops it under pressure instead of compressing/swapping it (or other apps); a lookup takes it back first and reads it again from flash if it was dropped. The budget follows what the kernel lets the cache keep (never below one token's cycle) and grows back once it stops dropping; the cache brake lowers it the same way and keeps the configured size as the ceiling. New files `moe/discardable_entries.{h,cpp}`. Host test with every offered entry dropped before reuse: answers identical.

- **Fix: Gemma (sliding window) answered in another language / "decode failed" after Regenerate or an edit.** llama.cpp's sliding-window cache accepts any cut, but after rolling back hundreds of tokens the window before the cut was already evicted, so the SWA layers held a broken context (log: "inconsistent sequence positions"). The prefix reuse and `keep_kv_prefix` now check the window like the llama.cpp server (`pos_min <= n - n_swa`, `pos_max == n - 1`) and otherwise restore a context checkpoint or re-prefill.

- Mouse right-click in the chat input (also while editing a message) opens Cut / Copy / Paste / Select all / Share / Search the web at the pointer (`TextFieldWithMouseMenu`). Tool results (e.g. Termux output) have a Copy button and can be selected when expanded; notices and the live command output can be copied too.
- Loading asks only when there is a real risk (RAM, a fixed cache over 60 % of RAM, pinned weights, a suspiciously small file) or an error. The notes "regular (non-MoE) model" and "Guess ahead pauses for image turns" no longer open the dialog, so with n-gram on by default a model loads with one tap.
- Defaults: Guess ahead is n-gram (exact at any temperature, costs nothing when nothing repeats) and "prefer cached experts" is 15 %. Existing settings are kept.

- Models page: the model list is sorted by last use (the chat's model menu too); MTP drafters, LoRA adapters and vision projectors are listed below the models and show where the file is. - Agent: the model is asked to keep scripts short (no comments or extras; a one-line command for a one-off step), and gets the last 1000 characters of a command's output (was 1500).
- Expert cache sizes in finer steps: 250 MiB up to 2000, 500 MiB up to 5000, then 6000/7000/8000; the Auto cap in 1000 MiB steps from 1000 to 8000. The auto-tuner picks from the same finer list.

- Guess ahead (MTP / n-gram) works with any temperature. Drafts are verified by DRAWING the target's token with the turn's own sampler at each position (the draft stays while the draw equals it, the first differing draw is the next token), so every token is a sample from the model's distribution exactly as without guessing; the engine no longer refuses spec + sampling (config.cpp) and the app no longer forces temperature 0 when guess ahead is on (it did so silently). The API server honours client sampling with guess ahead on as well. Fewer drafts are accepted at higher temperatures.
- Tool calls are written greedily: once the output contains `<tool_call>`, the rest of the turn is drawn at temperature 0 (the trigger is now sent whenever tools are enabled, also on reasoning turns without the grammar), so a call's name and JSON are the model's most likely tokens while the chat text before it keeps the chosen temperature. `ToolGrammarSampler::sample(logits, greedy)`; host test case (b2).

- The approval for replacing a file says Replace / Cancel (it said Delete); approvals can name their own button (`ConfirmationRequest.confirmLabel`).
- Fix: the approval dialog for a tool call often did not appear and the call waited forever (only with Approval *Ask*). `GenerationManager` changed its state with a plain read-modify-write from several threads; the "tool started" event, arriving at the same moment as the approval request, overwrote it. State changes are now atomic (`MutableStateFlow.update`), and the tool-started event keeps the approval line when the request came first.

- Approval in the chat's status row: while a tool waits for approval the row says "Waiting for your approval…", shows what is to be approved (e.g. the Termux command and folder) and has Accept / Reject right there, in addition to the dialog. Before, the row looked like a running command ("Termux: …" with a clock and Cancel) while the call was in fact waiting for an approval dialog the user did not see; Cancel then declined it and the model read that as a refusal. The tool's clock now starts once the call is approved. Found through the new command history: the "hanging" commands had never reached Termux.

- Agent prompt: an ENVIRONMENT block comes first — Android tablet, not Windows/macOS/a Linux server (no PowerShell, cmd, sudo, /root, /mnt/data), no built-in Python or sandbox, everything runs through run_shell in Termux, with an example call `python3 …`. Models had tried PowerShell (Mellum) or Python outside Termux (LFM2.5). The app also asks Termux what it offers (architecture, Python, pip, bash; `RunShellTool.ENVIRONMENT_PROBE`, at most daily after an agent run and on *Test Termux*) and puts the answer into the prompt ("Checked in Termux on this device: …"), so the model does not reinstall Python. The cached answer (`.bigmoe/termux-env.txt`) is only rewritten when it changes, so the prompt and the engine's cached context stay stable. Cancelling a command now tells the model that the user stopped a stuck command, not that they refused it.

- The switches under the chat input (Thinking, web search, file/code/utility tools, Termux) are kept per chat (`ChatComposerDataStore` "toggles:<chat>", `ChatToggles`): an agent chat keeps its tools, a story chat keeps them off, switching chats no longer changes them. A new chat starts with the switches last used; they move to the chat when its first message is sent. A chat from before this change takes the current switches the first time it is opened. Deleting a chat removes its switches.

- Model folder (Models page, top): every GGUF in a folder — default `Internal storage/Models`, changeable with Android's folder picker or switched off — is listed automatically and used in place, without registering or copying each file; two levels of subfolders are scanned, hidden folders and unfinished downloads skipped. Drafters are recognised by name, LoRA adapters by their GGUF header (cached per file), projectors as before. Needs all-files access (a Grant access button is shown). Deleting such a model in the app is refused with a hint to delete or move it in the folder, so the app never deletes your files. New: `ModelManager.modelFolder/setModelFolder/resetModelFolder`, test `modelFolderListsItsGgufsInPlaceByKind`.
- `mellum` (JetBrains Mellum MoE) added to the MoE streaming registry (standard `ffn_{gate,up,down}_exps`, no shared expert); before, loading one failed with "no MoE recipe for architecture 'mellum'".

- run_shell results are small: the model gets only the END of a command's output (errors and results are there), 1500 characters for stdout and stderr together (stderr gets up to two thirds), cleaned of colour codes, progress-bar redraws and blank lines; the header says how much there was. Before, the general 3500-character limit kept the beginning and cut the end. Commands run with `PIP_PROGRESS_BAR=off`, `PIP_NO_COLOR=1`, `NO_COLOR=1`; the prompt asks for quiet options and a short check at the end, and to write long output to a file and look at it with tail/grep.

- Agent: when the model writes `<tool_response>` itself after its call (it then invents a result, e.g. "/usr/bin/python3: can't open file '/root/x.pdf'" from a Linux sandbox it knows from training), the app stops the generation there, drops the invented part from the chat and the saved message, runs the real tool and re-sends the history next round. The prompt says Termux is not a Linux server (no /root, /mnt/data, sudo), never to write `<tool_response>`, and to take Python libraries with C code from Termux packages (`pkg install python-pillow`) instead of compiling them with pip. A cancelled command's result now says it did NOT complete and includes its output so far. Every command is recorded in `<workspace>/.bigmoe/history/` (command, folder, start, whole output, how it ended; newest 50). Chat model menu: own rows instead of Material3 menu items (capped at 280 dp), so names stay on one line and the menu is as wide as the longest name allows (a name longer than the screen scrolls sideways).

- Agent reliability (from testing on the tablet): run_shell commands get no input (`</dev/null`, `PIP_NO_INPUT=1`, `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`), so a prompt fails at once instead of hanging until the time limit, and Python output is unbuffered (`PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`), so it shows while the script runs. The wrapper also writes the exit code to a file: when Termux's answer does not arrive (Android paused Termux), the result is read from the files after 5 s; when Termux does not start a command within 20 s, the tool reports that Termux is not responding and marks the command so it never starts late. `termux-wake-lock` is held during an agent run and released at its end (`Tool.onRunFinished`). The chat shows the running command's whole output folded under the status line (tap "Output" to unfold, follows the end like a terminal), the time limit next to the elapsed time and "no output for N min". Cancel now shows "Stopping…" at once and also works while a call waits for approval (it is then declined); it still ends only that call, and the model gets "Error: Cancelled by the user …" and decides how to go on (Stop ends the whole run). The prompt tells the model to answer only after the last tool result and to name files by their workspace path. Tests: real-bash tests for closed input, a lost answer and a Termux that never starts; AgentControllerTest for a cancelled call going back to the model.

The "Publish release" workflow now creates the release as a draft and publishes it in a second call (three tries); a draft left behind by a failed run is reused instead of stopping with "already exists", and errors show as annotations on the run page.

If the device cannot run it for that model (a quantized V cache needs flash attention), the model loads with F16 and says so.
- Models page: model cards collapse (tap the name); collapsed cards show what is attached (MTP, Vision, LoRA, KV type). The loaded model starts expanded.
- Chat model menu: as wide as the screen allows and full model names (wrapped, not cut), so two quantisations of the same model can be told apart; a split model also shows its real file name.

- Agent feedback from first tests: (1) with Termux on, the prompt tells the model to use run_shell on its own for anything that needs running code or making files, instead of showing code or asking; (2) it checks before installing and installs only what is missing, in one command (`command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || pkg install -y ffmpeg`, `python3 -c 'import x' 2>/dev/null || pip install x`); (3) the chat shows what is happening: "Writing create_file: story.txt…" while the model writes a (hidden) tool call, "Termux: <command>…" with elapsed time and the last line the command printed while it runs, "Reading the result…" afterwards, and result cards titled "Termux · exit 0 ✓" / "exit 1 ✗" / "cancelled"; (4) a Cancel button next to a running tool ends just that tool (the model gets "cancelled" and goes on); Stop now also ends a running tool instead of waiting for it. run_shell runs commands through a small wrapper that records the pid and copies the output into `<workspace>/.bigmoe/` (hidden), so a cancelled or timed-out command and all its child processes are stopped in Termux (TERM, then KILL). New `run_shell` tool (Settings → Tools → Termux, and the chat's wrench menu): runs `bash -c` in the separately installed Termux app through its RUN_COMMAND intent (keys from termux-shared's TermuxConstants), background app shell, working folder inside the shared workspace, result (exit code, stdout, stderr, original lengths) back through a mutable PendingIntent to `termux/TermuxResultReceiver`. Per-call wait 5–1800 s (default 120); a command that does not answer in time keeps running in Termux and the model is told so. Termux's own errors (allow-external-apps off, storage) come back with the fix. Manifest: `com.termux.permission.RUN_COMMAND`, `<queries>` for com.termux, the receiver. - Grammar-checked tool calls (Settings → Tools → Agent, on by default): a lazy llama.cpp grammar (`parser/ToolGrammar`, `core/src/engine/tool_grammar.cpp`) switches on at `<tool_call>` and only lets the model write a valid call to an enabled tool (JSON object arguments, closing tag, then end of turn). Works with MTP / n-gram Guess ahead (drafts are verified through the grammar), never feeds llama.cpp a token that would abort it, skipped on turns that reason first. New `GenerateRequest::tool_grammar` / `tool_grammar_trigger`, JNI `nativeGenerate(…, toolGrammar, toolGrammarTrigger, callback)`. Details in docs/tool-calling.md.

- Shared workspace folder (Settings → Diagnostics & workspace → Workspace → "Shared workspace folder"): moves the workspace from app-private storage to `Internal storage/BigMoe/workspace`, so Termux (after `termux-setup-storage`) and other apps with storage access can work on the same files, e.g. through a link `~/bigmoe -> ~/storage/shared/BigMoe/workspace`. The move copies first and deletes a source file only once its copy is byte-identical; a different file already at the target is kept as "<name> (before move)"; files written during the move are picked up by a second pass. Artifacts and attachments stay linked because the database stores workspace-relative paths. A `.nomedia` marker keeps gallery and music apps out and is hidden from listings and the AI's file tools. Turning the switch off moves everything back. If all-files access is taken away later, the app opens the private workspace at its next start and says so in Settings; the shared files are left untouched. New: `workspace/WorkspaceMover.kt` (pure, JVM tests in `WorkspaceMoverTest`), `core/WorkspaceSwitcher.kt`, `ui/settings/WorkspaceSettings.kt`; `Workspace.relocate()`; FileProvider path `shared_workspace`.

Removing the gates alone would have been unsafe, so the engine was also fixed: the MTP draft pass during prefill ran while the target's weights were rebound to the device (and with the arena hooked in), and the MTP head's layer, experts and KV were pulled into the device rebind. A button on every page lists the texts shown there. Tap one: a local model translates it (pick and load one if none is loaded), you can edit the result, and Apply writes it into the language in use (a template for the device language is made first if there is none). Turn off when done.

A dense table the model only reads a few ROWS from per token (the token embedding) does not need to be in RAM: only the rows are read, from flash. Lossless - the output is identical. On a model where no table qualifies this does nothing. Not used while NPU prefill is on for the model (the two do not combine): a model's card can switch its NPU off.
A language is a JSON file in {0}: the English text as key, the translation as value. Missing texts stay English.

A resident expert costs no read, so a bigger cache means less waiting on flash, paid for in RAM. With Auto this is the minimum the cache grows from. A model's card can set its own. Speed tip: every reply shows its cache hit rate ("cache NN%") in its stats line; a low rate means flash is what slows you down.

After the app finishes a web search, automatically fetch a few related images and include their preview cards in the conversation. Adds network time and tool-result tokens; requires Allow image search.
All-files access is currently off. The app falls back to private storage at its next start.
At higher thresholds, more layers use routed reads; a lower threshold chooses a full-layer read sooner. This is a memory-I/O trade-off, not a quality setting.
Bets a layer reuses the previous token's experts and reads them on idle lanes. Needs the cache.
Bypass the page cache, so the system keeps no second copy of what the cache already holds. Falls back where unsupported.
Commits each layer's routing that many layers early, so its reads start early and can never be wasted. Lossy: some slots route differently. Excludes the prefetchers and Guess ahead.

Consult fewer experts per token than the model asks for. Cuts compute and reads together, and changes the reply. Speed tip: fewer experts means fewer flash reads per token. Lower it one step at a time (a model that routes 10 can try 6) and compare the answers with the model default.
Create folders and files, read, search, edit, rename, delete, zip. Everything stays in this chat's files.

Decode only, decided before each answer, no reload. The decode cores chosen above are the START value: a model opens with them, then Auto moves both ways. While the skin temperature is low, Honor's throttle step is calm and the last answer kept (almost) all its threads busy, one more core, the fastest one not in use, is added. When it gets hot or Honor throttles, or a core did not work, the slowest core in use is taken away (never below 2), also one of the cores chosen above. The title bar shows the temperature, the cores and how many of them worked ("busy"). Needs a device that reports its skin temperature.
Decode writes the answer one token at a time (this sets the t/s), prefill reads your message before the answer

Drops every token that is less likely than this fraction of the best token. 0.05 = a token needs at least 5 % of the favourite's probability. Cuts the nonsense tail when the model is sure, keeps choice when it is not. 0 = off.

How many of the most recent tokens the three penalties look at. 64 = roughly the last sentence or two. 0 = all penalties off.
How many tool rounds the AI may chain in one answer (install, write, run, check, fix, ...). When it hits the limit it stops; say "continue" to let it go on.

How random the choice of the next token is. 0 = always the most likely token (greedy, repeatable, good for code and tool calls). 0.6 to 0.8 = natural chat. Above 1 = more surprising, but more mistakes. Top P, Top K and Min P only matter above 0.
If no dialog appears: App settings → Permissions → Additional permissions → "Run commands in Termux environment".
Ignore the temperature / top_p / top_k, thinking and max_tokens that clients send and use this app's own settings instead.

Implemented: file attachments and reading, workspace/artifacts, file/code/utility/web tools, image/video attachment plumbing with mmproj support, thinking and web toggles. Voice input is not part of this project.
Import takes .md and .txt files; a .zip (a Notion export) goes into a subfolder named after it, emptied first, with only its text files.
Keeps only the K most likely tokens before drawing. 40 is common. 0 = off (no limit). A hard cap; Top P and Min P adapt to how sure the model is.
Keeps only the most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to this share, the rest is never picked. 0.9 = the top 90 % of the probability. 1 = off. Lower = safer, more predictable wording.
Lets other apps on this phone (for example Mobile Harness running Claude Code) use the model that is loaded here,

Lets the model look up how this app and its engine work (settings, expert cache, tools, NPU, API server) in the documentation, change log and setting texts bundled in the app, offline.
