Loader, threshold and routed-read preferences do not activate hardware by themselves. They stay disabled until the runtime can open HTP0.
Log: what llama.cpp and the engine print while loading and generating (timings, cache, I/O, errors). Off until you switch "Record log" on there. Filter it, copy it or share it as a file.
Lowers a token by a fixed amount once it appeared at all in the window, however often. Nudges towards new words and topics. 0 = off, 0.1 to 0.5 is gentle.
Lowers a token more the more often it appeared in the window (each repeat counts). Against overused words. 0 = off, 0.1 to 0.5 is gentle.

Makes every token that already appeared in the repeat window less likely, by this factor. Against loops (the same sentence over and over). 1 = off, 1.05 to 1.15 is typical; higher bends wording and can break code, names and JSON.

Minimum controls how exact a repeated suffix must be before n-gram drafts; maximum bounds the lookup work. Works with any temperature: guesses are checked by drawing with your sampling settings, so the answer is the same kind of text as without guessing.

More tokens per pass only pay off when most of them are accepted. Speed tip: with a model that streams its experts from flash, a pass over several tokens reads the experts of all of them, so the gain is uncertain. Compare tokens per second with and without it; a model that ships its own MTP head (Qwen3.8 Flash Next) is worth one try.

Once every weight has been copied into the app's own memory, the model file does not need to stay mapped. Lossless - the output is identical. Needs Dense weights on Anon or Pinned. Leave it off for a model with a lazily read n-gram table (Qwen3.8 Flash Next): that table is read through the mapping.
One request runs at a time. The in-app chat has priority: if you send a message while an API request is running, that request is cancelled (HTTP 529 / overloaded).

Order in the engine: penalties, then Top K, Top P, Min P, then temperature and the draw. Sampling is sent with every chat message, so changes need no reload. The penalties also work at temperature 0, but the engine leaves them out while the model runs with Guess ahead.
Predict which experts a prompt graph needs and load those instead of reading every expert in the layer. Falls back to a full-layer read when the predicted routing is dense.

Publishes the first projection's expert reads before queuing the remaining projections, allowing I/O lanes to start earlier. Experimental; requires expert streaming, cache, and overlap. Leave off if it is slower on your device.
RAM window used to keep recently accessed rows. Larger windows reduce repeated reads but leave less RAM for experts and the OS.
Recommended: Paper, Pearl, Mint, Graphite and Ocean. Custom palettes stay saved on this device.
Retention only reads nothing and just protects what the prediction names, which is the safe setting.
Runs the next layer's own router a layer early and prefetches what it names. More accurate than the bet above, and replaces it. Needs the cache.

Saves a chat's context when you switch to another chat, reload or unload the model, or leave the app, and loads it back when you return: the conversation continues without prefilling it again. Stored in the app's own storage, oldest removed first above 6 GB. Tied to the model file, KV type, LoRA and draft setup.
Search and analyse source files, and run JavaScript in an offline sandbox to compute or test.
Send it as  x-api-key: <key>  or  Authorization: Bearer <key>. A new key stops working clients until you update them.
Skin temperature as SamTweak shows it: Honor starts to throttle around 41 to 43 u00b0C. Between the two values nothing changes.

Skips a routed expert only when it is a cache miss and the router barely wanted it, so quality is spent only where it buys a read. A resident expert always runs and the top one is never dropped. Changes the reply, and not the same way twice: it depends on what the cache held. Speed tip: for a big model that streams a lot from flash this is a strong lever, because reads dominate. Try 50% first, then 75%, and check the answers.
Small caches may thrash and reduce performance. Enabled by default to preserve BigMoeOnEdge+'s existing behavior when one of the small cache sizes is selected.
Stops an MTP draft early when the drafter's confidence in its next token is below this. A message with an image is answered without drafting. A separate drafter adds its weights to memory use.
The AI runs bash commands in Termux inside the workspace: Python scripts, pip/pkg installs, ffmpeg and so on.
The chat input offers these prompts; u2605 = new chats start with it. Changing a prompt makes the engine re-read the conversation once; the model stays loaded.

The model opens with the cache above. While more than the reserve below (plus the headroom) is free and none of the app lands in zram, the cache grows in steps (once it is full; step and pace are set below). When free RAM falls under the reserve or the app's zram grows, it shrinks again, also during an answer, never under the cache above. Everything it grew by is offered to Android: starting another app makes the system drop that part at once instead of compressing or closing apps.
The model reads everything a tool returns before it can continue, at the speed of prompt processing
The wiki lives in {0} and needs access to all files. Allow it, then tap Read the folder again.

These five apply at once, no reload. Faster growth (small step, short pace, low headroom) follows free RAM closely but moves memory more often; slower growth is calmer. A shrink takes back at least the amount above, more if free RAM is further under the reserve. The pause keeps the cache from growing right back into the pressure. The sampling pace is 2 s, so nothing reacts faster than that.
These options apply only when the APK includes the Hexagon backend. Prompt prefill can use the NPU; token-by-token decode remains on CPU.
This setting uses native Android UI components only. It does not generate or execute HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Interactive Artifacts are a separate feature for standalone HTML, SVG or Mermaid previews.

This share of the cache, the experts unused the longest, is offered to Android (MADV_FREE). The app does not decide when: the kernel takes offered pages when free RAM falls under its own thresholds, before it compresses anything into zram or closes an app, and for free. A dropped expert is read from flash again when needed. The rest is ordinary memory: Android can only move it into zram. The cache shrinks with what the kernel takes and grows back once it stops, but never under the share that is not offered. With Auto the share counts on the minimum; what Auto grew by is always offered. Off = ordinary memory.
Turn on "Shared workspace folder" under Diagnostics & workspace, otherwise Termux cannot see the files.

Upper bound for tokens computed in one graph while processing prompts; the engine caps this at the context size. Smaller values reduce reserved compute RAM and can leave more memory for expert cache; larger values can prefill faster but may cause memory pressure. Decode speed is generally unaffected.
Web search itself is switched on and off with the globe button in the chat.
Web search, image search, and web-page reading are controlled by the globe button in the chat. These tools are off by default.

When two experts score close, picks the one already in RAM. Same number of experts, fewer flash reads, faster decode. Changes the reply; 15% is the measured sweet spot. Speed tip: it raises the cache hit rate without reading fewer experts, so try 10-15% before Drop cold experts or a lower top-k.

Your own knowledge: import .md or .txt files or a .zip (a Notion export, notes, how-tos) into BigMoe/wiki below, or copy them there yourself (subfolders are fine), and the model searches them offline, before any web search. German and English both work. Only the best four passages reach the model, so a big folder costs no extra prompt time; keep it focused, though, unrelated files crowd out the right passages.
